newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's budget deficit fell sharply in February.
newsitem.headline: Israel's budget deficit fell sharply in February.

text.p: The Israeli government's budget deficit fell sharply in February to 561 million shekels, preliminary figures released by the Treasury on Monday show.
Note: Figures are in millions of shekels. They do not include credit granted.
The deficit compared with an adjusted 1.41 billion shekel deficit in January, which had elicited calls from the Bank of Israel for immediate budget-cutting measures.
The Treasury said the domestic deficit was 106 million shekels, down from 1.16 billion shekels in January, while the foreign deficit rose to 455 million shekels from 251 million shekels.
The deficit was for the first two months of the year came to 1.97 billion shekels the Treasury said, compared with a full-year projected deficit of approximately 9.74 billion shekels.

"We expect that from the start of the year until the receipt of economic aid from the government of the United States towards the end of the year, the cumulative (foreign) deficit will be covered by the aid," the Treasury said.

The Treasury added that it had absorbed 931 million shekels of liquidity during February, or 881 million shekels since the start of the year. During the month the Treasury raised 1.09 billion shekels in the domestic bond market, about the same as in January.
